rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Society of Northwest Suburbs of Chicago (ISNS) serves as a central religious and social hub for the local Muslim community. founded in 1974, the organization provides <cite id="1">daily and Friday congregations</cite> alongside essential life-cycle services such as <cite id="2">marriages and funeral services</cite>. Its operations are primarily funded through <cite id="3">contributions totaling $3,982,043 in FY2023</cite>. While the organization maintains a <cite id="4">high program expense ratio of 92.5%</cite> according to its most recent filings, it faces significant financial management questions. Specifically, the charity holds <cite id="5">117.3 months of working capital</cite> in working capital. This level of reserves is considered excessive for a non-profit, particularly one that <cite id="6">accepts zakat donations</cite> intended for prompt distribution to the needy. Furthermore, the organization experienced a <cite id="7">revenue decline of 10%</cite> in the most recent fiscal year, dropping from $4,092,615 in FY2023 to $3,697,122 in FY2024. This financial contraction, paired with a <cite id="8">77/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, suggests a period of transition or stabilization rather than growth. Despite these fiscal complexities, ISNS remains a vital provider of <cite id="9">Islamic education for children</cite> through its Sunday School and Al Safa Academy programs.
